text.p: German chemical group Sued-Chemie AG said on Tuesday that a strong start to the year led it to expected higher sales this year while profits would match those posted last year.

Sued-Chemie chief executive Juergen Kammer said group sales climbed by nine percent while parent company sales climbed by 4.8 percent in the first quarter. Kammer said profits were clearly better, declining to comment further.

Last year group sales climbed by 7.6 percent to 1.1 billion marks, largely driven by the acquisitions of the Airsec SA and Waverly Mineral Products Corp. The group's operating result climbed to 102.9 million marks from 91.8 million marks in 1995 and net profit climbed to 51.9 million marks from 41.3 million marks.
Kammer also said the group could be eyeing more takeovers, saying "We are ready if interesting opportunities present themselves."
